title: Fuzzy granulation improves wind-speed forecasts in three Penglai site datasets
summary: A fuzzy-information-granulation ensemble combines neural predictors for wind-speed forecasting. On three 10-minute-resolution Penglai wind-farm datasets (7,110 observations per site, split 5:2 for training and testing), reported one-step MAPE was 7.86%, 5.18%, and 14.56% for the three datasets. These are held-out results from the study data, not prospective wind-farm operating outcomes.
ai_technology: Fuzzy-information-granulation ensemble with multiple neural predictors and multi-objective tuna-swarm optimization
organization: Macau University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: Three 10-minute-resolution datasets from different Penglai wind-farm sites, each with 7,110 observations and a 5:2 train/test split. The designed system reported one-step MAPE of 7.86%, 5.18%, and 14.56% across the three datasets.
evidence.unknown: The evaluation uses held-out data from one wind farm; prospective operating outcomes and validation at other wind farms are not established in the reviewed material.
evidence.ai_role: Fuzzy-information-granulation preprocessing and a multi-objective optimizer combine forecasts from multiple neural predictors.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
